metadata.note: The Minneapolis, Northfield and Southern Railway (MN&S), a new South Dakota corporation that on 6 August 1918 bought the foreclosed property of the Minneapolis, St. Paul, Rochester and Dubuque Electric Traction Co. - the 'Dan Patch Line' - and ran its passenger trains until the last run on 30 April 1942, then carried on as a freight belt road (Soo Line 1982, merged 1986). Drawn from research/branches/minneapolis_northfield_and_southern_railway.txt in the site repo (DanielMConnolly/historical-trains), researched 2026-11-03. Before this layer the map drew nothing for this company. Five features, one colour, one company: the main line split at Auto Club (where the High Line meets it), the High Line shuttle, and the two runs over Chicago Great Western track to Mankato and Randolph, which are MN&S trains and so MN&S colour on CGW geometry. Everything before 6 Aug 1918 belongs to the predecessor's own layer, not this one. Never electrified (gas-electric motor cars, trailers, some steam), so intercity_rail rather than interurban under Rule 7.

metadata.freight_only: Rule 1 exclusions. (1) The whole system after 30 April 1942 - MN&S freight belt road to 1982, Soo/CP, Progressive Rail and CPKC today; every segment ends at 1942 or earlier. The 1943 'three or more round trips a day' quoted by the SLP Historical Society are freight trains. (2) The High Line after the shuttle (~1922): the rails survive as a Progressive Rail spur but no passenger service is known, so it is drawn only to 1921. (3) Northfield - Randolph and Northfield - Mankato MN&S freight rights after passenger service. (4) The 1927 Crystal extension (Golden Valley - Crystal, a freight connection to the Soo; the live CPKC 'MN&S Subdivision' north of Glenwood Jct) and the WWII Port Cargill spur near Savage: freight only, not drawn. (5) The 1911-12 Faribault extension grade was never completed.
metadata.horsecar: None. The road never used animal power.
metadata.rule_9: All features lie in Minnesota, inside US_BOUNDS.
metadata.ownership: No Rule 4 split inside this layer: every drawn span is MN&S-operated, 1918-1942 or shorter. The split from the predecessor Dan Patch company is 6 Aug 1918 (foreclosure sale to a new corporation, not a rename). Pence's Dec 1927 purchase of the Minnesota Western / Electric Short Line brought common control but separate corporations and separate trains - the Luce Line belongs in its own layer; only the 3.3 mi Glenwood Jct - downtown approach the MN&S used is drawn here.
not_yet_sourced: [OPEN] mns-high-line: the 54th St - Auto Club shuttle's end. Drawn to 1921, the last year implied by american-rails.com's note that railbus A-1 ran it until sold in 1922; whether any shuttle ran after that is unknown.

mns-northfield-mankato and mns-northfield-randolph: no primary MN&S-era (1918-1931) timetable or notice was found. Dates rest on Fowler's '1913>1931', the 18 Jan 1931 lease end and an uncited Wikipedia sentence; passenger service may have ended well before the lease. A 1920s Official Guide, Northfield News or Faribault Daily News notice would settle it.
mns-northfield-randolph start: Fowler implies 1913, the Dan Patch Corridor article says 1921 (drawn).
Frequencies after Dec 1918 and every avg_speed_kmh: estimates.
The Commission approved discontinuance 18 Feb 1941 but the last run was 30 Apr 1942; the 14-month gap is unexplained.

QUEUE OVERLAP: the predecessor queue entry (Minneapolis, St. Paul, Rochester and Dubuque Electric Traction / Dan Patch Line) is listed 1910-1942; it must end at 6 Aug 1918 or it will double-draw this layer.

properties.line: Minneapolis, Northfield and Southern: Minneapolis – Auto Club
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not measured. No MN&S-era running time was recovered (research report UNRESOLVED 7); 40 km/h is the order of magnitude for an all-stops gas-electric motor car on this kind of road, nothing more (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror, cached degree tiles) plus OpenHistoricalMap (CC0), routed with opstrace.py. No OSM way carries old_railway_operator for this road (probed MN&S / MNS / Northfield / Dan Patch: zero hits); the MN&S survives instead under name= ('MN&S Subdivision', 'Minneapolis Northfield & Southern', 'Dan Patch Line'), so the Operator was widened to read name/operator on OSM ways too, and OHM ways named 'Dan Patch Line', 'Minneapols [sic] Northfield and Southern Railway', 'Electric Short Line Railway' and 'Minneapolis, St. Paul, Rochester and Dubuque Electric Traction Company' were costed 1x; untagged track 1.25x; trails 3x; other named operators 12x. Waypoints were placed on the mapped track (Nominatim answers checked by type: Faribault came back as Faribault County and was not used; Cannon Lake came back as the lake). Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals; no out-and-back spurs.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap and OpenHistoricalMap: 17.19 mi drawn against the documented 17.6 mi (Fowler line 130, Minneapolis MP 0.0 to Auto Club MP 17.6). ONE STRAIGHT-LINE LEG, approximated: 0.45 mi from the end of the mapped Electric Short Line grade (44.9791,-93.2881) to the downtown terminal at 7th Street & 3rd Avenue North (pinned at 44.9818,-93.2797, accurate to about a block - sources disagree between 2nd and 3rd Avenue North, report UNRESOLVED 4); the final approach is redeveloped and appears in neither OSM nor OHM. The first 3.2 mi (terminal - Glenwood Junction, documented 3.3 mi) follow OHM's 'Electric Short Line Railway' way - ESL/Minnesota Western track the MN&S used under lease - and Glenwood Jct - St. Louis Park follows OHM's 1915 Dan Patch cut-off ('Minneapolis, St. Paul, Rochester and Dubuque Electric Traction Company'), mostly within 40 m of surviving CP/BNSF track; about 0.3 mi near (44.977,-93.352) has no mapped way within 40 m and is drawn on the OHM grade alone. South of St. Louis Park it is the live CPKC 'MN&S Subdivision' (12.2 mi) and Progressive Rail track to Auto Club. ERA: this is the 1915 St. Louis Park cut-off alignment, which is the route MN&S trains used 1918-1942; no later realignment is known on it, though the present-day track and yards are drawn where they coincide with the grade.

segments.note: MN&S main line, north end: downtown Minneapolis (7th St & 3rd Ave N terminal) - Glenwood Jct (first 3.3 mi over Electric Short Line / Minnesota Western track under lease) - St. Louis Park - Edina - Bush Lake - Auto Club. The MN&S bought the foreclosed Dan Patch Line on 6 Aug 1918; downtown passenger trains resumed 25 Nov 1918 [SLP Hist. Soc.]. Last passenger run 30 April 1942 (Minneapolis Morning Tribune via SLP Hist. Soc.; MNopedia gives the same date); the Warehouse & Railroad Commission had approved discontinuance 18 Feb 1941. Never electrified despite the predecessor's 'Electric Traction' name: gas-electric motor cars and trailers, some steam. Freight continued as a belt road (MN&S to 1982, then Soo/CP; Progressive Rail and CPKC today) - not drawn. headway_min 720 is the Dec 1918 timetable's 2 round trips daily (plus 2 more each way on Sundays) [SLP Hist. Soc.]; no 1920s-30s frequency was found, so 720 for those years is an ESTIMATE carried forward from 1918.
sources: Segment-level: 1918 acquisition and 25 Nov 1918 resumption, 30 Apr 1942 last run and the Dec 1918 frequency are each cited for this line by the sources below; the post-1918 headway is an estimate.

segments.note: MN&S main line, south end: Auto Club - Savage (Minnesota River crossing) - Orchard Gardens - Antlers Park - Lakeville - Eureka Center - Northfield, connecting there with the CGW, Rock Island and Milwaukee Road. Operated by the MN&S from its 6 Aug 1918 purchase of the Dan Patch property (Mankato Free Press 6 Sep 1918: 'The entire line of the Minneapolis, Northfield and Southern railway, formerly the "Dan Patch," is to be operated'); the last passenger run, on 30 April 1942, was 'a trip to Northfield' [MNopedia], photographed at Lakeville. The Feb 1952 Official Guide prints the MN&S station list with no times and daggers every MN&S station as freight - consistent with the 1942 end, not used to date it. headway_min 720 = Dec 1918 timetable's 2 round trips daily Minneapolis - Northfield [SLP Hist. Soc.]; later years are an ESTIMATE carried forward.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap and OpenHistoricalMap: 9.82 mi drawn against the documented 10.2 mi (Fowler line 131, 54th St MP 0.0 to Auto Club 10.2). ONE STRAIGHT-LINE LEG, approximated: 0.77 mi from the north end of surviving track near 61st St (44.8950,-93.2833) to the 54th St & Nicollet Ave terminal (pinned at 44.9055,-93.2780); that stretch is lifted and redeveloped and is in neither OSM nor OHM, and the straight leg is most of the 0.4 mi shortfall. The rest follows the live 'Dan Patch Line' / CP / Progressive Rail High Line spur south through Richfield and west through Bloomington; a 0.16 mi join at the west end runs from the spur's last mapped vertex to the Auto Club point on the main-line feature. ERA: the original 1910 Dan Patch route as it survives today; the north end beyond 61st St is approximated as above.

segments.note: The original 1910 Dan Patch route into the city, reduced after the 1915 St. Louis Park cut-off to a stub served by a shuttle from Auto Club to the TCRT streetcar transfer at 54th St & Nicollet. Drawn from the MN&S takeover in 1918; american-rails.com's roster note says railbus A-1 (31-seat White, built 1918 in the company shop) 'ran this route until it was sold in 1922'. [OPEN] END: 1921 is the last year safely implied, NOT a known end of service - the 1922 sale is the disposal of a vehicle, not a dated end of the shuttle, and nothing found says whether anything replaced it. Do not extend without evidence, and do NOT draw this to 1942 with the main line: the rails survive as a Progressive Rail freight spur, but no passenger service on them after the shuttle is known. headway_min 480 is a GUESS; no shuttle timetable was found.
sources: Segment-level: secondary sources only, no timetable - the 1918 railbus and the 1922 sale are cited for this shuttle by american-rails.com; the end is [OPEN] and the headway is a guess.

properties.line: Minneapolis, Northfield and Southern: Northfield – Mankato (via Faribault)
properties.speed_source: ESTIMATE, not measured. No MN&S-era running time was recovered (research report UNRESOLVED 7); 40 km/h is the order of magnitude for an all-stops gas-electric motor car on this kind of road, nothing more (Rule 3).
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (mail.ru mirror) plus OpenHistoricalMap (CC0), routed with opstrace.py on the CHICAGO GREAT WESTERN alignment: OSM and OHM ways naming 'Chicago Great Western', its predecessor the 'Wisconsin, Minnesota and Pacific Railroad', or the Sakatah Singing Hills State Trail (the CGW Mankato branch grade) costed 1x, untagged track 1.25x, other named operators 12x, so the trace could not stray onto the parallel Milwaukee Road or M&StL. Douglas-Peucker 8 m, then trim_reversals; no out-and-back spurs. Starts at the same Northfield vertex as the MN&S main line so the features meet.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap and OpenHistoricalMap on the CGW alignment: 53.52 mi drawn against the documented 51.5 mi (Fowler CGW line 39, Northfield MP 52.1 to Mankato 103.6), 3.9% long - the Mankato end runs to the north side of the city (44.1799,-94.0012) and the exact CGW Mankato station used by MN&S cars was not established. ONE STRAIGHT-LINE LEG, approximated: a 0.16 mi join at Northfield from the MN&S main line's end vertex to the CGW. Northfield - Faribault follows OHM 'Chicago Great Western' (12.4 mi way) over surviving/abandoned OSM track; Faribault - Mankato is the abandoned CGW (ex-Wisconsin, Minnesota and Pacific) grade, now the Sakatah Singing Hills State Trail (about 34 mi), with OHM's 'Wisconsin, Minnesota and Pacific Railroad' ways filling Madison Lake - Mankato; about 1.3 mi has no mapped way within 40 m. FOREIGN TRACK: this is Chicago Great Western railroad drawn in MN&S colour because the MN&S ran these passenger trains; the CGW's own service on the branch is not drawn here. ERA: the CGW line as last mapped before abandonment; no realignment between 1918 and 1931 is known.

segments.note: MN&S gas-electric passenger cars over the Chicago Great Western's Mankato branch: Northfield - Dundas - Faribault - Tower City (an MN&S-only stop) - Cannon Lake - Waterville - Elysian - Madison Lake - Mankato (Northfield Depot Museum timeline: MN&S 'passenger service with gas-electric cars' on CGW track 'from Randolph through Faribault to Mankato'). Drawn from 1918, when the MN&S took over the Dan Patch company's operation (the Mankato running itself began in 1913 under the predecessor, which in 1915 ran seven daily trains Minneapolis - Mankato). Dates are LOW CONFIDENCE and rest on John Fowler's 'service Randolph-Mankato operated by Minneapolis Northfield & Southern (MNS) 1913>1931' (CGW line 39) and on the CGW lease ending 18 January 1931 (american-rails.com); 1931 itself is not drawn because the lease ended in its third week, and the lease end is a ceiling - passenger trains may have stopped earlier. NO MN&S-era (1918-1931) timetable or newspaper notice was found: a full-text search of the Mankato Free Press 1919-24 found nothing either way. headway_min 720 is a GUESS; no MN&S-era frequency was found.

ONE STRAIGHT-LINE LEG, approximated: a 0.31 mi join at Northfield from the MN&S main line's end vertex to the CGW, which is most of the excess. The rest follows the surviving 'Cannon Valley Line' track and OHM/OSM 'Chicago Great Western' ways to the junction with the CGW Chicago - Twin Cities main line at Randolph. FOREIGN TRACK: Chicago Great Western railroad drawn in MN&S colour because the MN&S ran these passenger trains. ERA: the line as it survives; no realignment known.

segments.note: MN&S passenger trains over CGW trackage rights Northfield - Waterford - Wallace - Randolph, meeting the CGW Chicago - Twin Cities main line. START IS CONFLICTED: Fowler's CGW line-39 note implies MN&S running from Randolph since 1913, while the Dan Patch Corridor article says (uncited) the line reached Randolph under a CGW lease 'in 1921'; the later date is drawn. Dates are LOW CONFIDENCE and rest on John Fowler's 'service Randolph-Mankato operated by Minneapolis Northfield & Southern (MNS) 1913>1931' (CGW line 39) and on the CGW lease ending 18 January 1931 (american-rails.com); 1931 itself is not drawn because the lease ended in its third week, and the lease end is a ceiling - passenger trains may have stopped earlier. NO MN&S-era (1918-1931) timetable or newspaper notice was found: a full-text search of the Mankato Free Press 1919-24 found nothing either way. Whether passenger (rather than freight) trains ran to Randolph at all under the MN&S is asserted only by the Northfield Depot Museum timeline and Fowler. Freight rights survived to the 1968 CGW-C&NW merger; the Feb 1952 Official Guide heads Randolph - Northfield 'Freight Service only' - a Rule 1 exclusion, not a passenger end date. headway_min 720 is a GUESS.
